key_facts: The Wall Street Journal published a story on Wednesday about security instructions AI labs give employees, including OpenAI's advice to consider whether someone seducing them could be a spy.
The FBI arrested OpenAI employee Abdulrahman Alfozan and charged him with bugging a lab conference room; he was fired and has not entered a plea.
WSJ reporter Erin Woo posted the OpenAI line on X, setting off jokes about tech workers and spies.
Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, joked that Meta's Superintelligence Labs office is in the South Bay.
Others joked that the advice was the best recruiting strategy or a hit to employees' self-esteem.
quote_evidence: Reporter Erin Woo wrote on X: "OPENAI to EMPLOYEES: If someone is trying to seduce you, first consider — could they be a spy???"
"This is now my favorite 2026 burn," wrote Ashley Mayer, the cofounder of the venture capital firm Coalition.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows how AI-lab security worries after an alleged bugging case are playing out as internet humour.
notes: BI reports memes; underlying security-advice story is the Wall Street Journal's, not read.
title: The internet is roasting tech bros with memes about seductive spies
